_note: Source-of-truth for orchestrator loops. ALL loops are on-demand — no cron fires automatically. Entry point: operator triggers master; master decides at runtime which sub-loops to run, in what order, and which to parallelize. optimization and build-maintain-cycle require separate explicit operator triggers. Loops that FIX follow the SHARED FIX CONTRACT in docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md > 'Shared fix contract'.

loops.label: Stabilization (bug-fix before features)
loops.attendance: on-demand — driven by master or triggered standalone; attended; commit-on-green, pause-on-gates
loops.prompt: Stabilization loop tick — BUG-FIX BEFORE FEATURES (operator directive). Do NOT start new feature/ROADMAP feature work. (0) CI HEALTH GATE — always first: run `gh run list --branch master --limit 3 --json conclusion,name,createdAt`. If all recent runs show conclusion=success, proceed. If any are red: CI fix is P0 regardless of ROADMAP priority. Identify the failures: `gh run view <latest-id> --log-failed | grep FAILED`. Run the exact failing tests locally BEFORE committing any fix (python3 -m pytest <failing-test-path> -x). NEVER pin a dep or revert a change on circumstantial evidence alone (e.g. a dep released on the same day as the failure is correlation, not causation — reproduce locally first). Apply the SHARED FIX CONTRACT (docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md > 'Shared fix contract') to the root cause. Log outcome to ci_health in .claude/loops/loop-runs-state.json: set master_status to "green" | "red" | "fix-in-flight", append newly identified failing_tests (dedup), set last_checked to current ISO date. Only advance to step (1) when CI is green OR a tracked fix is in-flight (committed this tick, CI queued). (1) DISCOVER (bounded — cap context), in priority order: (a) BURN DOWN THE FILED BACKLOG FIRST — grep docs/goal/ROADMAP.md for open `[ ]` `P1`/`P2` items tagged `T:backend:pending` (esp. codebase-review-/maintenance-filed findings like IMP-04x); these are already triaged work that the review loops file faster than anything fixes, so close them before hunting new bugs. SKIP any item whose body says DESIGN DECISION / intent-dependent (those need an operator call via AskUserQuestion, not a fix). (b) run `/builder-test ledger` to sweep docs/goal/TESTING.md pending/S:fail rows in the matching phase (read at most ~15 rows). (c) `/code-review` on the current diff / recent changes (compact). (2) FIX each REAL bug or best-practice finding via the SHARED FIX CONTRACT (docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md > 'Shared fix contract'); on green, flip the TESTING ledger token to passed. (3) Stop when no in-scope bugs remain. If nothing actionable, report "stabilization: clean this tick". Route per docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md; python3 not python; argv-style Bash; never edit a managed-app workspace.

loops.label: Maintenance (mine orchestrated-agent sessions, propose-only)
loops.attendance: on-demand — driven by master or triggered standalone; unattended; propose-only, never applies runtime/prompt edits
loops.prompt: Maintenance loop tick — PROPOSE-ONLY. Dispatch the session-maintainer subagent (.claude/agents/session-maintainer.md) to mine the Builder's ORCHESTRATED-agent sessions (project prefixes -tmp-aab-workspaces-*, -tmp-devpulse-*, -tmp-claude-*-aab-workspaces-*) over the last 24h using scripts/mine_sessions.py --errors-only (and builder logs analyze where useful). The miner now sweeps nested subagents/ transcripts and reports lane_coverage. COVERAGE GUARD: read lane_coverage + scanned_projects and reconcile against `builder agent sessions --limit 100 --json` — if the builder ran sessions in a lane the miner could not see (codex_sdk writes nothing to ~/.claude/projects), report that as an explicit COVERAGE GAP; never emit a clean 'no blockers' / 'no new sessions' for an unscanned lane. Classify each recurring blocker by root cause into permission / env / tool-schema / sandbox / code-test, with counts and distinct sessions. PROPOSE minimal fixes at the owning surface (execution_policy.py for permission_mode/dontAsk; quality_gates/python_env.py for env; agent-prompt tightening for tool-schema/sandbox), each proposal quoting the VERBATIM current source line (re-read at propose time; no memory anchors) — but do NOT apply any runtime-policy or agent-prompt edit; surface the diffs to the operator for approval. DEDUPE before filing: list open `builder backlog item ... --source validation` and skip signatures already tracked (reference the id) — only file genuinely new findings via `builder backlog item create --source validation` (incident/improvement/optimization) and propose `builder memory add` for new reusable patterns. DEP CURRENCY SWEEP — run: `python3 -m pip list --outdated --format=json`. Cross-check each result against pyproject.toml [project].dependencies: (a) PINNED dep (has an upper bound, e.g. <0.26) with a newer version available → flag as "pinned-dep-upgrade-candidate: test before unpinning"; file as improvement backlog item if not already tracked. (b) UNPINNED dep (only a lower bound, e.g. >=0.12.0) whose latest available version is a MAJOR or MINOR version jump from currently installed → file as incident via `builder backlog item create --source validation` immediately; cite the typer 0.26 case (38 tests broken silently, dep unpinned — INC filed 2026-06-25) as the class exemplar in the body. Do NOT propose any pins, upgrades, or pyproject.toml edits — this sweep is flag-and-file only; version changes require local test evidence and operator approval. (c) ANTHROPIC SDK PACKAGES — if anthropic, anthropic-ai, claude-sdk, or related SDK packages have a new MINOR or MAJOR version available, additionally file an improvement backlog item: "capfit-currency refresh recommended — new SDK version <X> available; run the capfit-currency procedure to update capability-fit skill + rubrics from live docs." This replaces the retired capfit-currency loop as the trigger mechanism. If no outdated deps: note "dep-currency: all deps current". If coverage is complete and no new blockers, report "maintenance: no new blockers (lanes: <lane_coverage>)" and stop; if a lane was unscanned, report the COVERAGE GAP instead of an all-clear.

loops.label: Optimization (autonomously advance one efficiency/cost IMP end-to-end to a propose-at-PR gate)
loops.attendance: on-demand only — trigger manually; do NOT arm via CronCreate (it builds features = high-cost, must be attended). Orchestrator-led; autonomous through SELECT+BUILD+VERIFY+VALIDATE; STOPS at an operator approval gate (propose-at-PR). Never auto-merges or pushes to master unattended.
loops.prompt: Optimization loop tick — ON-DEMAND, ORCHESTRATOR-LED, ATTENDED, PROPOSE-AT-PR (never auto-merge or push to master). Goal: autonomously advance ONE efficiency/cost-optimization ROADMAP item end-to-end, stopping at an operator approval gate. Steps: (1) SELECT (bounded) — read docs/goal/ROADMAP.md; from the OPEN `[ ]` items pick the single highest-leverage EFFICIENCY/COST/TOKEN optimization item (e.g. IMP-028 code-gen context replay ~89% of run cost; IMP-027 complexity-proportional SDLC; G13 effort carve-out; G14 OTel). Prefer the largest stated cost leverage that is not blocked. If a prior tick left an in-flight optimization branch, RESUME it instead of starting new. If no open optimization item, report "optimization: none open" and stop. Do NOT touch non-efficiency features (those belong to the stabilization/feature lanes). (2) BUILD (isolated) — create an isolated git worktree/branch, NEVER build on master (see docs/workflows/git-worktree-best-practices). Dispatch planner (architect the change: owner-surface checks, test-sync, risks) -> implementer (code + tests in the SAME change). Keep changes bounded to the selected item; cross an owner boundary only if the plan requires it and call it out. (3) VERIFY correctness — dispatch test-sync-verifier (pytest + ruff + the touched builder quality-gate + test-sync grep). If the change touches frontend/ or the embedded dashboard, ALSO dispatch browser-verifier for live proof. Correctness MUST be green before proceeding; if red, route back to implementer to fix at root (bounded retries), else stop and surface the blocker. (4) VALIDATE the saving — it is an optimization, so PROVE it saves. If autoresearch is ACTIVE (docs/autoresearch/baseline_runs.tsv is non-empty), run the autoresearch Iterate lane (/autoresearch -> Iterate) on the relevant fixture(s): the saving MUST clear the 2-sigma baseline floor with NO gate_pass_rate regression to count as VALIDATED. If autoresearch is still ACTIVATING (baseline empty), do NOT block — capture a saving ESTIMATE via `builder logs analyze --session <id>` (token/cost delta, now accurate post-IMP-023) on a before/after run, and FLAG the proposal "saving ESTIMATED — statistical validation PENDING autoresearch baseline; run /autoresearch Baseline to enable". NEVER claim a validated saving without the 2-sigma evidence. (5) PROPOSE-AT-PR gate — STOP. Commit ON GREEN to the isolated branch ONLY (no push to master, no auto-merge). Surface to the operator via AskUserQuestion an evidence bundle: which IMP, diff summary, correctness result, and the saving (validated 2-sigma delta OR estimate + pending-flag). On approval, open the PR (gh) / push the branch; on hold, leave the branch intact for the next tick to RESUME. NEVER merge or push to master unattended. Route every step per docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md. Use python3 not python; argv-style Bash; never edit a managed-app workspace; the main thread owns commits/PRs and the approval gate.

loops.label: Build -> Maintain -> Fix cycle (dogfooding flywheel; self-contained build-drive; writes stay with main thread)
loops.attendance: on-demand only — orchestrator-led, attended. The MAIN THREAD is the SOLE writer: it runs the builder-test + maintenance loops as steps, reviews propose-only findings, and applies root-cause fixes itself in an ISOLATED worktree. Subagents NEVER touch git (implementer.md git guard).
loops.prompt: Build -> Maintain -> Fix cycle — ON-DEMAND, ORCHESTRATOR-LED, ATTENDED. The dogfooding flywheel; the main thread orchestrates. One iteration: (1) BUILD + OBSERVE (no source fixes here). PRECONDITION: a builder server is up (`builder --json doctor`; it serves on :9876 by default while the CLI defaults to :8000 — prefix EVERY builder CLI call with `AAB_API_URL=http://localhost:<port>`); read + RECORD the lane (only claude is minable; codex_sdk = COVERAGE GAP). BOARD CHECK (do this BEFORE driving anything): `builder board show --json` + scan `blocked`/`failed` columns and `blocked_reason` — a pre-existing blocked/failed task is the highest-value signal; diagnose and triage it BEFORE submitting any new feature build (it may already be the root-cause defect the flywheel is hunting). CHOOSE TARGET: a running instance is bound to ONE app (driving its dashboard only EXTENDS that app — correct, not a bug). For a NEW app, PROVISION first: fresh `~/Builder-Workspace/<name>` + `builder init --no-input --project-name <name>` + `builder start` on its own --port, THEN drive ITS dashboard; for CONTINUE, drive the running instance. DRIVE: dispatch a RUN-ONLY browser driver (`browser-verifier`), NOT the self-fixing `/builder-test` skill; bridge `diagnose` first (BAIL ~2 min if it hangs — tooling, not your job); submit the build instruction; OBSERVE to completion OR the STUCK watchdog (max_turns / no progress ~10 min / stranded). CAPTURE: verdict, session ids + project prefix, lane, FRICTIONS OBSERVED (observation-fact vs speculation; builder-product vs driver/tooling). (2) MINE — run the `maintenance` loop (PROPOSE-ONLY) scoped to this sprint's sessions (`--project-filter` the prefix); honor its COVERAGE GUARD; if the build STUCK, mine the hung session IMMEDIATELY. (3) TRIAGE -> FIX -> COMMIT: apply the SHARED FIX CONTRACT (docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md > 'Shared fix contract') over BOTH signals — the mining AND the driver's FRICTIONS OBSERVED (a clean mine is NOT 'no frictions'; operator-experience frictions live outside transcripts). RETROACTIVE RECOVERY: if the source fix corrects a scaffold/generator defect, any existing managed-app workspace generated by the old code is still broken — after committing the source fix, check the board for blocked tasks whose `blocked_reason` matches the defect signature; if found, also manually apply the workspace-level fix (update the generated file in `~/Builder-Workspace/<app>/`) AND recover via the dashboard before claiming the iteration done; a committed source fix without a recovered dashboard = incomplete evidence. (4) VALIDATE BY NON-RECURRENCE (two modes): agent-internal signatures are validated when the NEXT build's mining shows the transcript SIGNATURE GONE; operator-UI/behavior frictions are validated by a DELIBERATE REPRODUCTION that recreates the trigger and shows it fixed. Record each fixed friction + its validation mode; recurrence after a fix = symptom patch -> reopen. (5) LOOP — start the next sprint (step 1) so the fixed friction is re-tested; stop when the operator pauses or no recurring root cause remains. Route per docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md; python3 not python; argv-style Bash; never edit a managed-app workspace.

loops.label: Codebase review (review EXISTING code by slice, fix at root — watermarked; correctness + clear-quality only)
loops.attendance: on-demand — driven by master step-3 or triggered standalone; attended; main thread sole writer; one bounded slice per tick
loops.prompt: Codebase-review loop tick — ON-DEMAND, ORCHESTRATOR-LED, ATTENDED. Review EXISTING code one bounded slice per tick and fix at root. (1) SELECT SLICE — read the watermark `.claude/loops/codebase-review-state.json` (slice -> last-reviewed sha; create `{}` if absent); pick the next slice that is unreviewed OR changed since its sha, prioritized by RISK (largest / most-central / most-depended-on / hottest-churn; M1.3 god-files are top risk). ONE bounded slice per tick = a module/subsystem or one large file + its tests; cap context, never load the whole repo. (2) REVIEW — the built-in `/code-review` is DIFF-scoped, so dispatch a RUN-ONLY reviewer that READS the slice's existing files and applies the code-review rubric (~/.claude/docs/workflows/code-review.md), returning findings SEVERITY-TAGGED: IMPORTANT (correctness/safety) | QUALITY (high-confidence dead-code/dedup/reuse) | NIT/OPINION (omit). (3) TRIAGE -> FIX -> COMMIT: apply the SHARED FIX CONTRACT (docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md > 'Shared fix contract'). Structural god-file DECOMPOSITION is OUT — defer to M1.3; this loop does bounded IN-PLACE fixes only. (4) WATERMARK — update `codebase-review-state.json` slice -> current sha so the next tick advances and never re-reviews an unchanged slice. (5) RECORD — report slice reviewed, findings by severity, FIXED vs FILED; if no confirmed Important/Quality issue, record the slice reviewed-clean and advance. Route per docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md; python3 not python; argv-style Bash; never edit a managed-app workspace.

loops.label: Master orchestration (adaptive — assess, plan, execute, retrospect)
loops.attendance: on-demand — operator-triggered; attended; sole writer = main thread; decides at runtime which sub-loops to run, in what order, and which to parallelize; does NOT run optimization or build-maintain-cycle (those need explicit separate triggers)
loops.prompt:
Master loop tick — ATTENDED, MAIN-THREAD SOLE WRITER, OPERATOR-TRIGGERED. You are the adaptive orchestrator. You assess current state, decide at runtime how to route the sub-loops, then self-introspect to encode learnings for future agents. Sub-loop prompts are authoritative in .claude/loops/loops.json — read each by id before executing it; do not restate inline.

PHASE 1 — ASSESS (always first; parallelize all four reads as concurrent tool calls in one message):
(a) CI health: `gh run list --branch master --limit 3 --json conclusion,name,createdAt` + read ci_health from .claude/loops/loop-runs-state.json
(b) Watermarks: read .claude/loops/loop-runs-state.json — which sub-loops haven't run (null or >7 days for stabilization/maintenance/codebase-review, >7 days for hygiene)?
(c) Open work depth: `grep -c '^\- \[ \]' docs/goal/ROADMAP.md` + skim the first 5 open P1/P2 items
(d) Recent friction: `builder agent sessions --limit 10 --json` — scan for error patterns, hangs, repeated failures from the last 24h
Synthesize (a)–(d) before moving to phase 2.

PHASE 2 — PLAN (state routing decision in 3–5 lines before executing anything):
Decide: which sub-loops to run this tick, in what order, and which to parallelize. Decision rules:
- CI RED → P0; run stabilization's CI-fix path immediately; hold everything else until CI is green or fix-in-flight.
- CI GREEN, stabilization stale, maintenance stale → dispatch maintenance as a BACKGROUND SUBAGENT (Agent tool, run_in_background=true) while the main thread finishes any remaining assessment work; collect its proposals before dispatching stabilization.
- CI GREEN, stabilization current (ran today), maintenance stale → maintenance only.
- codebase-review slice sha unchanged since last watermark → skip; don't waste a tick on a no-op.
- No open P1/P2 items AND stabilization ran today → skip stabilization; report 'stabilization: current'.
Maintenance is ALWAYS safe to parallelize (propose-only, never commits). Stabilization and codebase-review are SEQUENTIAL — they both commit; never run both concurrently. State the plan explicitly (e.g. 'CI green; dispatching maintenance in background; will run stabilization after proposals land; codebase-review: skipping — slice unchanged').

PHASE 3 — EXECUTE (adaptive — deviate from the plan when evidence demands it):
Run each sub-loop by reading its prompt from loops.json by id. After each COMMITTING sub-loop finishes, RE-ASSESS ci_health before starting the next (state may have changed).
Maintenance proposals in context before stabilization: when maintenance produces proposals naming specific files/functions, incorporate those as higher-confidence targets when stabilization selects what to fix (session-backed evidence > speculation).

MID-RUN SELF-INTROSPECTION — when master encounters unexpected friction (wrong hypothesis, CI surprise, missing context, misrouted fix, repeated revert): STOP at that moment. Diagnose root cause. If the friction is non-obvious or would recur for future agents: immediately file a backlog item (`builder backlog item create --type improvement --source validation`) OR propose a loop-prompt edit via AskUserQuestion — then continue with the corrected approach. Do NOT defer encoding to phase 4 while context is still rich.

PHASE 4 — RETROSPECT (always, even if no sub-loops ran):
(a) DECISIONS — what routing choices did you make and why? Were any wrong in hindsight?
(b) FRICTION LOG — what slowed you down or caused confusion? (missing state, stale watermarks, ambiguous prompts, bad CI read, wrong assumption before evidence)
(c) PATTERN ANALYSIS — mine sessions generated THIS tick: `builder agent sessions --limit 30 --json` filtered to sessions started after this tick began. Group findings across sub-loops: CI/env failures in multiple loops, wrong-diagnosis patterns (hypothesis→revert→correct-fix), dep/pin gaps (unpinned dep that jumped a version), enforcement blind spots. For any pattern found in ≥2 distinct sessions this tick: `builder backlog item create --type improvement --source validation --title 'Recurring: <pattern-name>' --description '<verbatim evidence + session ids>'` (dedup against open items first). Propose `builder memory add` for novel patterns not yet in builder memory.
(d) ENCODE — any durable learning from this tick not yet filed in (c): propose `builder memory add`.
(e) SELF-OPTIMIZE FOLD-IN — if the 'hygiene' watermark in loop-runs-state.json is > 7 days old, run /self-optimize (clustering lane) over dev sessions from the last 7 days: cluster recurring operator corrections into ranked themes, map each to its owning surface (.claude/agents/ prompt / AGENTS.md / skill SKILL.md / tests/conftest.py), PROPOSE targeted edits (do NOT apply), append genuinely new durable learnings to project memory. Update the 'hygiene' watermark.

WATERMARK UPDATE — write to .claude/loops/loop-runs-state.json only for sub-loops that actually ran this tick. Set master to today's ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Update ci_health.last_checked + master_status ('green'/'red'/'fix-in-flight'). Leave unchanged any sub-loop that was skipped or failed — let it re-trigger next tick.

Route per docs/workflows/orchestrator-routing.md Shared Fix Contract for all fixes. python3 not python; argv-style Bash; never edit a managed-app workspace.
